top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock rests on one clean mechanism, the magic-wavelength condition that cancels the lattice light shift, followed by a quantitative programme in which blackbody, collisional and lattice shifts were measured and cross-checked. It has been reproduced and surpassed independently in Tokyo, Boulder, Paris, Braunschweig and elsewhere, with clock comparisons agreeing near 1e-18, which is the reproducibility test I apply. The allocation to Katori (proposal and first demonstration) and Ye (accuracy and many-body regime) is uncontested, and a citation focused on the magic-wavelength lattice clock stays distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 single-ion prizes. An award is clearly better than no award.
